diagnostics.message:
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
`null_resource.delete_daemonset` runs `kubectl delete daemonset -n kube-system aws-node`, which removes the AWS VPC CNI only after Calico has taken over networking. The Calico chain ends at `null_resource.create_calico_installation` (apply_tigera_operator → kubernetes_secret.calico_image_pull → create_calico_installation), but `delete_daemonset` only waits on `null_resource.update_kubeconfig` and `module.eks`. If it runs before the Tigera operator/Installation exist, the cluster is left with no functioning CNI. It should be ordered after the Calico installation is created.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
null_resource.delete_daemonset removes the AWS VPC CNI (aws-node DaemonSet) from the cluster, but only waits for the cluster to exist (module.eks / null_resource.update_kubeconfig). This deployment uses Calico as the CNI (via null_resource.apply_tigera_operator → null_resource.create_calico_installation). The aws-node DaemonSet must only be deleted AFTER the Calico operator and Installation are in place, otherwise nodes lose pod networking. There is no attribute reference or depends_on linking delete_daemonset to the Calico installation resources, so Terraform may run the deletion before Calico is functional.
